output.segment: Residential price/value switchers currently on a competitor

research_questions.question: What is each competitor's actual serviceable footprint and advertised speed tiers in Ocala/Marion County specifically?
What are current standalone and bundled pricing tiers, promo rates, and post-promo rates for each competitor?
What early-termination fees, equipment/rental fees, and other recurring surcharges does each competitor charge?
What documented triggers cause residential customers to switch ISPs (promo-cliff bill shock, reliability, customer service, moving)?
How much does a bundled mobile plan influence purchase decisions for price/value switchers specifically?
What do verified customer reviews/complaints say about each competitor's pain points, prioritizing Ocala/central-FL sources?
How have other regional fiber ISPs without a mobile bundle positioned and priced against national cable/wireless incumbents?
What marketing channels are effective and cost-appropriate for a low-brand-recognition regional ISP in a mid-size FL market?

args.company_name: Industry switching triggers & mobile bundle influence
Ocala customer reviews and complaints compilation
Regional fiber ISPs (case studies without mobile bundles)

assumptions_and_gaps: Address-level serviceability (exact household availability) may require ISP address lookup tools or FCC mapping beyond these high-level tool calls; plan assumes API results will include Ocala/Marion County granularity.
Local Ocala/Marion County customer review volume may be limited; plan assumes regional sources (Ocala Star-Banner, Reddit r/ocala, BBB listings) will be used where direct local reviews are sparse.
Pricing, promo rates, and surcharges change frequently; plan will capture current advertised/public rates but not necessarily unpublished or time-limited offers.

Competitive footnotes (e.g., technician-install vs. self-install waivers) and exact ETAs for deployment may not be fully captured; further address-level validation or direct ISP contact would be required for absolute accuracy.
Some research questions (e.g., precise quantified influence of mobile bundles on switchers) rely on third-party studies; if local studies are unavailable, national/regional proxies will be used.
